nodes.label: AMPM Platform Requirements Audit (23 Oct 2026)
nodes.rationale: Establishes whether BIZ, WHY, SPEC and the two flowcharts are complete, consistent and precise enough to begin the SPEC §14 pre-development deliverables (wireframes, data model, permission matrix, technology recommendation, phased estimate); verdict: sufficient to start design under stated assumptions, not to start building.

nodes.label: BIZ: AMPM Website and App Business Explanation for Developer
nodes.rationale: Plain-language business brief, 9 sections, 21 Oct 2026; states that SPEC carries the detailed requirements; §9 lists decisions the developer must not assume.

nodes.label: WHY: Why AMPM App
nodes.rationale: Access model and customer funnel, 4 sections, 21 Oct 2026; the only document defining the demo/trial stage and the no-self-registration rule, and the rule that expiry never deletes wedding records.

nodes.label: SPEC: AMPM Developer Technical Specification v1.0
nodes.rationale: Primary specification (DOCX, 15 sections, 20 Oct 2026) generated with python-docx; no author, comments, tracked changes, revision history or sign-off, so its roles (§6), statuses (§7) and phases (§11) are treated as proposals until AMPM signs off (CF-7, RK-8).

nodes.label: TEAM-FLOW: AMPM App Visual Flowchart for team
nodes.rationale: Level-1 navigation for the team app (A3 PDF, undated); five tabs Home, Clients, Weddings, Tasks, More and one straight line from qualified client to closure; footer says detailed section workflows are to be designed next.

nodes.label: PORTAL-FLOW: AMPM Client Portal Visual Flowchart
nodes.rationale: Level-1 navigation for the client portal (A3 PDF, undated); four tabs Home, My Wedding, Approvals, More; client-facing access only; shows no hotel discovery.

nodes.label: Three distinct service stages: discovery, optional consultancy, full management
nodes.rationale: One stage never implies the next (the SPEC 'critical rule'); stated consistently in BIZ Step 5, WHY §1 and SPEC §1.2 and §15. Many clients stop at hotel discovery or consultancy and never get a wedding project, so the product must not be designed as a pure wedding-planning tool.

nodes.label: Server-side field-level protection of internal cost, margins, notes and identity documents
nodes.rationale: SPEC §4 security note and §6.1 explicitly reject hiding sensitive data only in the interface; internal commercial data must never leave the server, which is what prevents margin leaks through client-facing screens.

nodes.label: Approvals locked to exact versions of designs, menus and proposals
nodes.rationale: SPEC §5, §7 and §12: a decision applies to one exact version; a revision is a new version that needs a new approval.

nodes.label: Privacy by default for identity documents
nodes.rationale: Identity documents are never universally required; collection is conditional, restricted and audited (BIZ rule 7, SPEC §2.5, §5).

nodes.label: No hard-coded commercial rules
nodes.rationale: SPEC §10 and §13 and BIZ §9 keep prices, packages and policies configurable and list undecided policies explicitly instead of inventing them (BIZ rule 8: do not invent policies).

nodes.label: Concrete acceptance scenarios with tamper tests
nodes.rationale: SPEC §12 gives concrete acceptance scenarios including tamper tests on URLs, API requests and file links.

nodes.label: Phasing with exit criteria
nodes.rationale: SPEC §11 defines five delivery phases each with exit criteria; Phase 1's exit criterion is the lead-to-subscriber journey tested.

nodes.label: Not everything mandatory; parallel workflows allowed
nodes.rationale: BIZ rules 2 and 3 and SPEC §5 and §15: not all fields are compulsory and workflows may run in parallel.

nodes.label: Audit verdict: sufficient to start design under assumptions, not to build
nodes.rationale: SPEC is explicitly a starting specification and BIZ §9 and SPEC §13 leave commercial decisions open. Three problems stand out: the two flowcharts and the specification describe different products; the hotel database, the core of the subscription product, has no price field; and the commercial and access decisions that drive architecture (payment mode, one-time vs recurring, client-visible finance, native vs web, RSVP identity) are still open. Counts: 9 conflicts, 44 gaps, 15 ambiguities, 8 risks, 25 decisions for AMPM, 10 blocking design sign-off.

nodes.label: Demo or trial as a mode of the private platform
nodes.rationale: Recommended instead of a separate demo deployment: AMPM-provisioned demo accounts, an isolated seeded demo dataset, time-boxed access, delivered in Phase 1, plus a trial status. A separate deployment versus a demo tenant is an architecture and cost decision, and trial expiry needs automation that no document specifies.

nodes.label: Glossary and reconciled information architecture replacing the Level-1 flowcharts
nodes.rationale: Both flowcharts are usable only as navigation sketches for the full-wedding-management case; the reconciled architecture must add the subscriber-only client-portal state, the Hotels and Guests areas of the team app and the branching sales funnel, with one agreed glossary before Level-2 flows are drawn.

nodes.label: SPEC v1.1 amendments
nodes.rationale: Amend SPEC v1.0 with the no-self-registration rule, the no-deletion-on-expiry rule, a trial status, a price or rate-card entity, saved-hotel and room-block entities, the entitlement resolution rule and the missing status lists, and mark §6, §7 and §11 as proposals pending sign-off.

nodes.label: SPEC §14 pre-development deliverables
nodes.rationale: Ordered: entity-relationship diagram covering every module record in §7.1, role and permission matrix including field-level finance and guest-data restrictions, field matrix, wireframes, technical architecture, phased estimate; to start only after the Tier 1 decisions are resolved because the estimate depends on platform and sizing answers.

nodes.label: CF-1 Three environments vs four experiences
nodes.rationale: WHY §2 names three environments (public website, demo/trial, private platform) while BIZ §2 and SPEC §1.1 name four parts including the guest RSVP portal; the demo appears in SPEC only as one screen and one acceptance test and in no phase, so demo deployment versus demo tenant stays an architecture and cost decision.

nodes.label: CF-2 Client-portal flowchart omits hotel discovery
nodes.rationale: PORTAL-FLOW has Home, My Wedding, Approvals and More but no hotels area, search, favourites or assistance request, although hotel discovery is the Phase 1 product the subscription pays for; the Home countdown presupposes a wedding date, so the portal needs a subscriber-only state and an engaged-client state.

nodes.label: CF-3 Team flowchart hides Hotels and Guests
nodes.rationale: SPEC §2.4 lists nine team areas including Hotels and Guests; TEAM-FLOW's five tabs show neither except an undefined Database entry under More and Guest/hospitality inside Weddings, so the Hotel/Destination team and the RSVP/Guest team have no home and cross-wedding guest operations are not represented.

nodes.label: CF-4 Team flowchart shows one linear path with no subscription or consultancy branch
nodes.rationale: TEAM-FLOW runs qualified client, create wedding record, planning, live operations, closure in a straight line, contradicting the critical rule that many clients stop at discovery or consultancy; the Level-1 flow should branch after Clients into subscription, discovery, optional consultancy, optional engagement, project.

nodes.label: CF-5 Account creation and payment: no self-registration vs payment journey
nodes.rationale: WHY §3 and §4 say AMPM creates every account and there is no public self-registration; SPEC §2.1, §1.2 and §8 describe a payment journey that activates access and never state the no-self-registration rule. Online gateway with automatic activation versus offline payment with manual activation changes Phase 1 scope materially and blocks the Phase 1 exit criterion.

nodes.label: CF-6 Client-visible finance
nodes.rationale: PORTAL-FLOW commits to a client-facing budget and invoices and payment status while SPEC §2.3 limits clients to approved client-facing fields and SPEC §13 leaves the visible amounts undecided; the answer decides whether budget_lines and invoices need the client/internal split that vendor_proposals already has.

nodes.label: CF-7 Roles: proposal or decision
nodes.rationale: BIZ §9 says final user roles and data-access rules must not be assumed, yet SPEC §6 presents eleven roles as definitive and SPEC §13 omits roles from the pending decisions; SPEC §6 is therefore treated as the proposal, signed off through the role and permission matrix deliverable.

nodes.label: CF-8 Vocabulary that exists in only one document
nodes.rationale: Questionnaire, consultation as a tracked step, feedback and archive, schedule and calendar, messages and questions, countdown, Database and trial each appear in one document and are absent from SPEC; one agreed glossary is needed before Level-2 flows.

nodes.label: CF-9 Three distinct environments vs shared backend
nodes.rationale: WHY §2 asks for three distinct environments and SPEC §10 for a shared backend with separate user experiences; compatible only if environment means experience, which leaves the demo-data isolation level open (AM-8).

nodes.label: GP-1 Entitlement resolution across subscription, agreement and project
nodes.rationale: No rule says how subscription, service agreement and project permissions combine, what an expired discovery subscriber with an active wedding project sees, what a client sees after closure and for how long, or whether one subscription covers several weddings; WHY §4's rule that expiry and cancellation never delete wedding records is not restated in SPEC.

nodes.label: GP-2 Trial mechanics
nodes.rationale: No trial status among the SPEC §7 subscription statuses, no duration, no expiry automation, no demo dataset definition, no provisioning flow and no phase.

nodes.label: GP-3 Plans and packages: plan_id without a plans table
nodes.rationale: subscriptions.plan_id references a table that does not exist and there is no plan-to-module entitlement mapping although SPEC §10 requires configurable packages.

nodes.label: GP-4 One-time vs recurring subscription
nodes.rationale: No document says whether billing recurs; recurring billing adds renewals, failed-payment handling, proration and auto-expiry, a large scope item on its own.

nodes.label: GP-5 Hotel-assistance commercial flow
nodes.rationale: Request hotel assistance triggers paid services whose fees are undecided; the flow request, fee quote, agreement, work, status is not drawn and service_agreements has no status list or link from a hotel enquiry.

nodes.label: GP-6 Client payments for wedding milestones
GP-8 Hotel prices have nowhere to live
nodes.rationale: BIZ and SPEC require quoted prices with verification dates but SPEC §4 has no price, rate, quote or snapshot entity; Indian wedding hotel commercials need room rates by category and season, venue rental, per-plate food-and-beverage minimums, taxes and inclusions, which call for a rate-card or quote-snapshot entity with its own verification record.

nodes.label: GP-9 Availability has no entity or calendar
nodes.rationale: SPEC §12 says unverified availability is not shown as confirmed yet there is no availability entity; it should be stated as a per-enquiry manual check so the product does not promise live availability.

nodes.label: GP-10 Saved hotels, favourites and compare have no entity
GP-11 Room blocks not modelled
nodes.rationale: Rooms reserved per project, hotel, category and date are missing, so room_allocations cannot be validated against inventory and the rooming reports have no source.

nodes.label: GP-12 One hotel per wedding
nodes.rationale: wedding_projects.hotel_id is single-valued although destination weddings commonly use a main hotel plus overflow hotels and functions at venues outside the database; functions.venue is untyped.

nodes.label: GP-13 Guest atomic unit: individual vs family group
nodes.rationale: guests references a missing family_groups table, guest_function_attendance is per guest yet carries party_count, and allocations and travel use a polymorphic guest/group id; rooming and identity handling need individuals while headcounts need groups including children, so the individual guest must be the atomic record and the family group a grouping.

nodes.label: GP-14 Change requests have no entity, statuses or notifications
GP-15 Messaging and questions have no module
nodes.rationale: PORTAL-FLOW promises messages, questions and ask a question; SPEC has no messaging module, entity or notification, only design comments and guest tickets.

nodes.label: GP-16 Module records without entities
nodes.rationale: About 25 record types named in SPEC §3 have no table in §4 (budget categories, vendor categories, family groups, invitations, checklists, readiness checks, production items, artist bookings, departure records, lost-and-found, final account, notifications, configuration); the ER diagram deliverable must cover all of them.

nodes.label: GP-17 Payments and invoices lack direction, parties and client/internal split
nodes.rationale: payments has no direction, payer, payee or method and contracts/invoices has a single amount; if AMPM invoices marked-up vendor services this is a margin-leak path the §4 security note is meant to prevent.

nodes.label: GP-18 Tax: no GST fields
GP-19 Missing status lists and transitions
nodes.rationale: Twelve objects that carry state have no status list and no object has allowed transitions or transition permissions.

nodes.label: GP-20 Media rights for previous clients' wedding photos
nodes.rationale: Hotel profiles will show other clients' wedding photos and videos but documents/media has only a visibility field and no consent or rights fields.

nodes.label: GP-21 Vendor availability not modelled
GP-22 Bulk import and migration
nodes.rationale: No document mentions import; AMPM presumably has hotel research in spreadsheets and clients supply guest lists in Excel, and the hotel import decides whether Phase 1 launches with a populated database.

nodes.label: GP-23 Public website content management
GP-24 Dietary and allergy capture
GP-25 Guest list ownership
GP-26 Client-side users
nodes.rationale: Authorised family and decision-maker contacts imply several client users per wedding with different rights, but only one client role exists.

nodes.label: GP-27 Linking pre-project discovery activity to the wedding project
GP-29 Closure extras: feedback and archive
GP-31 Authentication specifics
nodes.rationale: No client sign-in method (email and password vs phone OTP), no password reset or account recovery, no multi-factor authentication for staff who see every client's finances, no session policy.

nodes.label: GP-32 Notifications
GP-33 Native app vs responsive web vs progressive web app
nodes.rationale: SPEC §10 says responsive web, both flowcharts say App with tab bars, BIZ says website and connected app, WHY says the private app; no document mentions iOS, Android, app stores or push notifications, and this decision alone can change the cost estimate by a large factor.

nodes.label: GP-34 Offline and low-connectivity use
nodes.rationale: Run-of-show, readiness checks and incidents will be used on phones inside hotel ballrooms and at outdoor venues, yet no document mentions offline behaviour.

nodes.label: GP-35 Sizing inputs
nodes.rationale: No numbers for team size, concurrent weddings, guests per wedding, hotels, media volume or subscribers; the SPEC §14 cost estimate cannot be produced responsibly without them.

nodes.label: GP-40 Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023
nodes.rationale: Guests are data principals who never contracted with AMPM; consent notice, purpose limitation, erasure, breach handling and a grievance contact must be designed into the RSVP portal.

nodes.label: GP-41 Aadhaar
nodes.rationale: The Aadhaar framework restricts private storage and use of Aadhaar numbers; recommended position is never to store them and, where hotels need identity for check-in, to keep only document type and a masked reference under restricted access with deletion after checkout.

nodes.label: GP-42 GST invoicing
GP-43 Hosting location and data residency
GP-44 Retention schedule per data class
AM-1 RSVP link model: shared wedding link vs per-guest token
nodes.rationale: A shared per-wedding link forces guests to identify themselves, creating privacy exposure and duplicate records that contradict SPEC §12; a per-guest or per-family token requires the guest list to be loaded before invitations go out.

nodes.label: AM-2 Function venue: foreign key or free text
AM-4 Material changes undefined
AM-7 Multiple approvers
AM-8 Demo data separation
nodes.rationale: Demo data must remain separate from real client data (WHY §4): a separate database or deployment, or a tenant flag in one database?

nodes.label: AM-10 Vendors and hotels as users
nodes.rationale: No role exists for vendors or hotels; vendor portals are a common later request and cheaper to plan for than to retrofit.

nodes.label: AM-11 Phase 1 consultancy depth
AM-14 Tenancy: AMPM only or future licensing
nodes.rationale: WHY calls the software a paid business asset, which could mean licensing to other planners; multi-tenancy is expensive to retrofit.

nodes.label: RK-1 Empty product at Phase 1 launch
nodes.rationale: Phase 1's value is a populated, verified hotel database, yet no document names a data source, data-entry plan, import tool or verification cadence; hotel data collection should start in parallel with design.

nodes.label: RK-2 Late financial-visibility decision forces rework
nodes.rationale: Margin model versus transparent fee changes budget_lines, invoices, payments and every client-facing finance screen; deciding after the Phase 2 model is built means rework and leak risk.

nodes.label: RK-3 App-vs-web decision not made before estimate
nodes.rationale: Native iOS and Android apps roughly double front-end effort versus responsive web, so the SPEC §14 cost estimate will be wrong without the decision.

nodes.label: RK-4 Guest communications lead time
nodes.rationale: WhatsApp Business API onboarding and template approval take weeks and must start early if WhatsApp, the dominant channel in India, is wanted; no document names a channel.

nodes.label: RK-5 Privacy exposure at scale
nodes.rationale: Each wedding adds hundreds of non-contracting data subjects; collecting identity documents, travel details and dietary data without a designed consent, retention and deletion model is a legal and reputational risk.

nodes.label: RK-6 Scope breadth
nodes.rationale: Fourteen modules, roughly fifty entities, eleven roles and five phases; Phase 1 must be scoped tightly or it will absorb Phase 2 features through the client portal.

nodes.label: RK-7 Divergent mental models between flowcharts and specification
nodes.rationale: If AMPM's internal picture is the flowcharts and the developer builds the spec, review meetings will surface the gap late.

nodes.label: RK-8 Unreviewed specification
nodes.rationale: SPEC was machine-generated with no author, comments or revision history; its roles, statuses and phases should be confirmed by AMPM before being treated as requirements.
